 By Shaghil Bilali , ET Online Last Updated: Oct 27, 2026, 12:28:52 PM IST Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis
 The National Confederation of Pensioners’ Associations has requested intervention from President Droupadi Murmu regarding higher EPS pension issues. They demand the withdrawal of a problematic EPFO circular that affects eligibility for pensions based on internal trust rules. In addition, they seek to halt unnecessary litigation and ensure uniform treatment for all retirees. The NCPA calls for waiving punitive interest related to administrative delays on pension claims. Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen ET Online Various higher EPS pension cases are pending at many High Courts and the Supreme Court. The National Confederation of Pensioners’ Associations (NCPA), an organisation that claims to represent 1 million pensioners from public sector undertakings (PSUs) and the private sector, has written to President Droupadi Murmu, seeking her intervention to resolve issues related to higher pensions under the Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) that impact lakhs of employees.
In a letter dated October 23, 2026, the NCPA has urged the President to direct the Ministry of Labour and Employment and the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation ( EPFO ) to stop “unnecessary” litigation regarding pending higher EPS pension cases and waive punitive interest and expedite the settlement of claims.
The NCPA has also requested the President to direct the EPFO to withdraw a circular dated January 18, 2025, in which the provident fund body said that the eligibility for pension in higher wage cases should have been determined based on the extant trust rules of the exempted establishments. 
Also Read: DA hike for central government employees: Can government announce dearness allowance increase on Wednesday? 
The NCPA says that, because of this circular, the EPFO is stopping many higher pension cases, citing that historical internal trust rules of an exempted establishment strictly mirrored the statutory wage ceilings.
 What NCPA says about higher EPS pension? 
The NCPA, in its letter, says that the government started the EPS in 1995 and established a framework for Pension of Higher Wages (PoHW) through a notification on February 28, 1996.
The NCPA argues that the Supreme Court’s landmark judgements in the RC Gupta (2016) and Sunil Kumar B (2022) cases settled the issue of the right to the higher EPS pension.
“Yet, the EPFO has chosen a path of active judicial defiance,” the NCPA says.
 Also read: EPS-95 pension row: Retirees challenge 2007 EPF amendment over lower pension; Karnataka HC rules against them 
In an earlier letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi last month, the NCPA had highlighted that in the EPFO Vs Sunil Kumar B. case in 2022, the Supreme Court explicitly ruled that employees of exempted and un-exempted establishments constitute ‘one single class’ for pension purposes.
 What are NCPA’s key grievances? 
· Requests to withdraw EPFO circular dated January 18, 2025 
The NCPA says that the EPFO’s January 18, 2025, circular says that the eligibility for pension on higher wage cases should be determined based on the extant trust rules of the exempted establishments, in consonance with the directions of the Supreme Court in the Sunil Kumar case in 2022.
The circular further says that in case the trust rules are amended, post the decision dated November 4, 2022, in the Sunil Kumar case, applications from members of such trusts may not be considered.
The NCPA says that the circular violates the Division Bench ruling of the Madras High Court (July 9, 2026), which affirmed that internal trust rules are merely administrative arrangements for the Provident Fund and cannot override parent legislation (under EPS-95 ) enacted by Parliament.
 Also Read: EPS-95: Private sector employees win higher pension case in Bombay High Court despite PF Trust wage ceiling limit cap; know why 
 Partial acceptance of higher EPS pension applications 
The NCPA says that while retirees from certain exempted and un-exempted establishments receive higher EPS pensions (with the Ministry of Labour admitting in Parliament on August 10, 2026, that over 149,806 PoHW orders were issued), retirees from selected exempted establishments face arbitrary mass rejections based on internal PF trust rules.
“This even creates hostile divisions within the same public sector undertakings (such as SAIL, HAL, BHEL, IOCL, HMT, BEL, ITI, and many more) based purely on geographical postings in different units under the same PSUs,” the NCPA, in the letter, says.
The NCPA here says that while employees of the same PSU get higher EPS pension at some centres, the same facility is not extended to employees at other centres.
“This violates Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution of India,” the NCPA says.
Also Read: No additional EPS contribution by government on higher wage ceiling of Rs 25,000; know what it means for your pension 
 Meagre pension, high court case expenditure 
The NCPA highlights that litigants are getting meagre pensions of Rs 2,000-Rs 5,000 a month while also fighting cases for higher EPS pensions.
“While the EPFO sits on an enormous pension corpus exceeding Rs 11 lakh crore, its litigious strategy has fostered a dark game of ‘attrition by mortality’, forcing senior citizens through endless court corridors,” the NCPA writes in the letter.
 Many litigations, no consensus on higher EPS pension 
The NCPA says that the EPFO’s current stance directly collides with the law of the land as settled by the Supreme Court and reaffirmed by multiple high courts.
The NCPA writes, “Post-Supreme Court verdict in 2022, there are about 400+ writ petitions and writ appeals pending in 18 high courts, and 26 judgments have already been delivered by 10 high courts covering more than 200 writ petitions in favour of the pensioners.”
 NCPA’s three requests to President Murmu 
The NCPA has requested President Droupadi Murmu to intervene and order the EPFO and the Ministry of Labour and Employment to take these three higher pension-related steps:
 A. Immediately withdraw the EPFO circular 
The NCPA has requested the “unconditional withdrawal of the oppressive and legally unsustainable EPFO circular” dated January 18, 2025.
 B. Halt litigation & enforce uniformity 
The NCPA has urged the President to conduct an immediate litigation audit to withdraw all frivolous appeals against settled high court judgements, ensuring that retirees of exempted establishments are not ‘subjected to structural or procedural discrimination.’
 C. Waive punitive interest & settle claims 
The pensioners’ body has requested the President to direct the acceptance of joint options for higher pensions without punitive interest penalties accrued ‘solely due to the EPFO’s administrative delays.’
The NCPA has suggested establishing a time-bound mechanism to grant immediate relief to ageing pensioners. ( Originally published on Oct 26, 2026 ) (Join our ETWealth WhatsApp channel for all the latest updates)
